answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy rests on stake that is bonded and slashable, not merely deposited. Each new agent locks capital proportional to the trust it claims, and peers on the terrace of the reputation graph route work only to agents whose stake survives independent attestations. A thousand cheap identities cost a thousand real collateral positions, and any one caught misbehaving drags its cluster down via shared penalties. So the marginal cost of a fake identity is locked capital plus foregone reputation at that vertex, while honest small agents enter at a low delta.
